name: Buildium
tagline: Cloud property management for landlords and managers: rent roll, accounting, tenant and owner portals, leasing, maintenance.

pricing.basis: monthly, priced by unit count with a plan minimum
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The rent ledger is the easy part: units, leases, recurring charges, payments, a late fee rule, a balance per tenant. That is a weekend of work and it genuinely covers a person with four doors who already knows their tenants. What does not survive the rewrite is everything attached to money moving and law: ACH and card rent collection with the attendant trust accounting rules, tenant screening pulled from credit bureaus, e-signed leases, 1099 and owner distribution reporting, listing syndication to the big rental portals, and a tenant portal your tenants will actually log into. You can replace the spreadsheet Buildium replaced, not Buildium. If you manage for other people's money, the compliance surface alone should keep you off a homemade build.
coreLoopDIY: A local app that tracks units, leases, recurring rent charges, manually recorded payments, late fees and per-tenant balances, and exports a rent roll and owner statement.
requirements: Your own bank, Zelle or payment app for actually collecting rent
Manual entry or bank CSV import for every payment
Separate arrangements for screening, e-signature and listings
Real bookkeeping discipline if you hold anyone else's funds
whatYouLose: Integrated rent collection and the reconciliation that comes with it
Tenant screening: credit, criminal and eviction history from the bureaus
Tenant and owner portals, plus the maintenance request flow tenants expect
E-signed leases, state-specific lease templates and listing syndication
Trust accounting, 1099 prep and owner distribution reporting that survives an audit
moatNotes: Managing property for someone else is a licensed, audited activity in most states. The software is cheap next to the liability it documents.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the product is not a ledger, it is a paper trail plus a payment rail plus a screening pipe. Collecting rent by ACH at scale means merchant and trust account plumbing nobody wants to own; screening means contracts with credit bureaus you cannot sign as a hobbyist; owner reporting means numbers that hold up when an owner or a state examiner asks. Add that tenants and owners are already trained on the portal, and switching away means retraining humans who did not ask to be retrained. For a landlord with two units, none of that matters. For anyone managing other people's buildings, all of it does.
notes: The rent roll is a weekend; the rails and the paper trail are not. The moat is regulated money movement plus bureau-fed screening plus reporting an auditor will accept.
prompt:
Build a local-only property management ledger for a small landlord. Stack: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Drizzle ORM. No auth, no cloud, no telemetry, single user on localhost.

Data model:
- properties: name, address, notes
- units: property_id, label, bedrooms, market_rent
- tenants: name, email, phone, notes
- leases: unit_id, tenant_id, start_date, end_date, monthly_rent, deposit_held, status (active | ended | upcoming)
- charges: lease_id, due_date, type (rent | late_fee | utility | other), amount, memo, generated_by (recurring | manual)
- payments: lease_id, received_date, amount, method (check | ach | zelle | cash | other), reference, memo
- maintenance: unit_id, opened_date, closed_date nullable, priority, description, cost nullable, vendor nullable
- documents: lease_id nullable, unit_id nullable, title, local_file_path, uploaded_date

Features:
1. Dashboard: total units, occupied vs vacant, rent expected this month, collected this month, outstanding balance, leases ending in the next 90 days.
2. A "post rent" action that generates this month's rent charge for every active lease, idempotent so running it twice does not double charge.
3. Configurable late fee rule in a settings table: grace days and either a flat amount or a percent of rent. A "apply late fees" action that posts fees for unpaid rent past grace, also idempotent.
4. Per-lease ledger page: charges and payments interleaved by date with a running balance.
5. Payment entry form, plus a CSV import that maps bank columns to payments and lets me match each row to a lease before committing.
6. Rent roll view: every unit with tenant, rent, lease dates, current balance. Export to CSV.
7. Owner statement: pick a property and a month, output income by category, maintenance costs, net, as a printable HTML page.
8. Maintenance log with open and closed filters.
9. Documents: store files under ./storage and link them to a lease or unit. No parsing.

Explicitly out of scope, do not stub fake versions: online rent payments, card or ACH processing, tenant screening, credit reporting, e-signature, listing syndication, tenant or owner login portals, email or SMS sending, accounting beyond cash in and cash out.

Seed the database with two properties, five units, four active leases and three months of history so every screen has data on first run. Any config goes in .env with a committed .env.example. Write a README with setup, the idempotency guarantees, and a short section stating this tool is not trust accounting software and should not be used to hold other people's funds.
